correctness.rationale: On each symmetry half the map has exactly \(k\) ordinary full affine branches of length \(1/\mu\) and a central full affine branch of length \(\theta/\mu\). Their total length is \(1\), so inverse change of variables proves invariant Lebesgue probability. Full-branch affine inverse cylinders have product measures; the contraction factor is at most \(1/\mu\), making the joint side/radial code generating and i.i.d. The weights factor into a fair side bit and the specified radial distribution. Shannon entropy then gives \(\log\mu-(2\theta/\mu)\log\theta\) and \(\log[2(k+1)]\) branch-shift entropy; differentiation \(k\log(1/\theta)/(k+\theta)^2>0\) and end limits establish the profile. The packaged exact-rational verifier passed 4,004 tested finite branch-word contributions and 156 inverse identities; infinite/all-real proof is analytical. Endpoints and even integral parameters are excluded appropriately.

value.rationale: The 2024 map is specifically proposed to produce threshold bits whose empirical statistics are tested. Exact i.i.d. block laws over every length and the resulting inability to identify the parameter from the stationary output law, together with an independent hidden radial process reveal which information a one-bit observer retains and which is invisible. The full parameter strip classification, strict metric/branch entropy gap, and its jump in the one-sided even-parameter limit distinguish two natural dynamical complexity quantities on a published applied map. This is a self-contained model-specific evaluation, not an arbitrary subcase or numerical sample. It does not infer pseudorandomness for fixed digital seeds or computational cryptographic security.
